relations.myth: Occupation of the mounds after the Milesian settlement
relations.note: Medieval narratives substantially overlap the Túatha Dé with the mound-dwelling Sídhe.
relations.source: De Gabáil in t-Sída; Lebor Gabála Érenn

relations.note: He distributes the mounds among the Túatha Dé and regulates fertility.

relations.myth: Winning Brug na Bóinne for a day and night
relations.note: He gains permanent possession of Brug na Bóinne through legal wordplay.
He receives Síd Rodrubán during the Dagda’s allocation of mound dwellings.
He receives Síd Aircelltraí during the Dagda’s allocation of mound dwellings.

relations.myth: Concealment and reorganization of the defeated Túatha Dé
relations.note: He assigns dwellings, raises supernatural concealment, and provides sustaining food.

relations.myth: Supernatural feast sustaining the mound society
relations.note: His feast or ale preserves the mound people against age and illness.
The ruler of Brí Léith repeatedly crosses between mound and human courts.
A mound-associated sorceress, she transforms and expels her rival Étaín.
She moves between mound society and mortality through transformation and rebirth.

relations.myth: Birth of Óengus at Brug na Bóinne
relations.note: She is associated with Brug na Bóinne and mothers Óengus in one version.
An earlier Brug resident, he is displaced through the Dagda’s and Óengus’s stratagems.

relations.myth: Cú Chulainn and the Otherworld war
relations.note: An Otherworld woman, she afflicts Cú Chulainn and later becomes his lover.

relations.myth: Recruiting Cú Chulainn for the Otherworld war
relations.note: She serves as envoy between Labraid’s Otherworld court and Cú Chulainn.

relations.myth: Cú Chulainn and the Otherworld war
relations.note: His Otherworld court recruits Cú Chulainn to defeat supernatural enemies.
Later systematization groups this independent supernatural woman with the Túatha Dé and Sídhe.
Later classification places Cú Chulainn’s divine father and helper among the mound people.
relations.source: Táin Bó Cúailnge; Compert Con Culainn

relations.note: He rules Síd ar Femuin and appears as a leading Túatha Dé king.
He emerges from a mound and burns Tara with magical music.
This Munster Otherworld woman was later included among regional fairy queens.
This Munster sovereignty figure was later characterized as a fairy queen.
His realm of the dead overlaps Sídhe Otherworld geography without universal kingship.
Later tellings sometimes group this shape-changing being with the fairy people.
Christian folklore sometimes explains the Sídhe as expelled or neutral angels.

relations.myth: Christian reinterpretation of Cú Chulainn’s visions
relations.note: A Christianizing coda reclassifies apparitions formerly called Sídhe as demonic deception.
